objective: Expand Chinese positive supervision with conservative seller-specific identity anchors instead of generic high-semantic overlap.

target_queue_size.note: This is a mining target, not a quota. If direct identity evidence is exhausted, the queue must remain smaller rather than dilute with generic semantic neighbors.

positive_split_targets.scientific_stop_rule: If direct positive anchors cannot reach these targets, do not claim few-shot should necessarily improve AUC; report target-domain identity evidence scarcity instead.

positive_component_closure.note: Closure-derived positives are not independent evidence units; they are retained for audit and excluded from primary supervision/evaluation counts.

buckets.review_notes: Positive anchor expansion: supplemental parser found the same low-frequency seller-contact handle in both profiles. Use positive only when the contact context is seller-facing rather than leaked victim data or parser noise.

Positive anchor expansion: existing pending Step 5 row has a direct contact/PGP field. Keep positive only if the shared identifier is seller-specific; use uncertain for victim-data emails or unsupported contact-only rows.

Positive anchor expansion: rare shared email/IM/phone/wallet identifier plus profile text or structural support. Use positive only when the identifier is seller-facing and not copied victim/product data.
Positive anchor expansion: rare shared external URL plus text/structural support. Treat as positive only when the URL is plausibly seller-operated identity infrastructure; otherwise uncertain.
Positive anchor expansion: cross-market uncommon alias plus direct identifier or content closure. Same-alias alone is insufficient; require additional seller-specific support.

Positive anchor expansion: the two sellers are connected by an already-reviewed clean positive component with no internal negative/uncertain contradiction. Marked separately because it is closure-derived rather than independent raw evidence.

positive: Use positive only for seller-specific identity anchors: explicit shared Telegram/Wickr/Wechat/Jabber/QQ/phone/wallet contact, PGP, seller-operated URL, or contradiction-free reviewed positive component closure.
A shared contact in leaked data rows is not a seller identity anchor.
A shared external URL is not a positive anchor unless context supports seller-operated infrastructure; public content links and file-hosting links are not sufficient.
A closure-derived edge is useful for audit closure only unless a future policy adds explicit train-only handling; it must not be counted as an independent test discovery.
uncertain: Use uncertain when the contact appears only in victim-data samples, public scraped rows, or one side lacks enough seller-facing context.
Use uncertain when the row is plausible but not defensible as a positive training label.
negative: Use negative only for clear parser noise or controller-distinct evidence.
Do not mark a contact row negative merely because the products differ.

hard_rules: Do not use generic high semantic similarity as a positive label.
Do not auto-promote victim-data contacts, public URL/parser fragments, exchange/file-host links, or high-frequency handles.
Append net-new candidate pairs to Step 4 only after this positive-anchor queue has been reviewed.
After applying reviewed labels, rerun Step 5 freeze.
Closure-derived rows must use candidate_scope=positive_component_closure_audit so they do not enter primary supervision/evaluation counts.
If the direct identity queue cannot reach the configured positive split targets, report evidence scarcity rather than claiming few-shot should improve AUC.
Because Step 4 may receive net-new pairs, rerun the full Step 7 preview and semantic feature pipeline before Step 7 training.
